chunks: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth al-Nakhaʿī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, Allah did not make the fasting of the month of Ramaḍān obligatory upon any of the nations before us.”
So I said to him: Then what about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you”?

He said: “Allah only made the fasting of the month of Ramaḍān obligatory upon the Prophets, not upon the nations. So He favored this community by it and made its fasting obligatory upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and upon his community.”

key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: the Prophets, upon whom this fasting was previously made obligatory
key_terms.الْأُمَمِ: the nations or communities before the Muslim Ummah
key_terms.الْأُمَّةَ: the Muslim community specially favored with this obligation
key_terms.شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, whose fasting is discussed as an obligation
key_terms.صِيَامَهُ: its fasting, meaning the fast of the month of Ramaḍān
key_terms.فَرْضاً: as an obligation, indicating binding religious duty
key_terms.كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ: has been prescribed upon you, indicating divine obligation

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explain the verse about fasting being prescribed for those before the Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the specific obligation of fasting the month of Ramaḍān was not prescribed for earlier nations in the same way it was for the Ummah of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It interprets the Qur'anic verse by distinguishing between the Prophets and their nations, presenting Ramaḍān fasting as a special divine favor granted to this Ummah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1844 - It is narrated by Sulayman ibn Dawood al-Minqari from Hafs ibn Ghayath al-Nakha‘i, who said:
"I heard Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)) say:
'Indeed, Allah (swt) did not make the fasting of the Month of Ramadan obligatory upon any nation before us.'
I said to him: 'Then what about the words of Allah (swt), the Almighty: "O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed upon you as it was prescribed upon those before you"?'
Imam (as) said: 'Allah (swt) made the fasting of the Month of Ramadan obligatory only upon the Prophets, not their nations.
He favored this nation and made its fasting obligatory upon the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) and upon his nation.'"
